name: Anah
overview: Anah was a male Edomite known as the son of Seir and a chief in Edom. He is noted in Scripture for discovering the hot springs in the wilderness, marking him as a figure of significance within the Edomite tribe. His leadership role and discovery highlight his importance in the Edomite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Anah appears once in Scripture without a specific meaning provided. It is a proper name mentioned in Genesis 36:20, and no additional titles or meanings are recorded.
familyAndRelationships: Anah is explicitly identified as the son of Seir, establishing a direct familial link within the Edomite genealogy. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record further family connections for Anah.
scriptureSignificance: Anah holds significance as both a son of Seir and a chief in Edom, indicating a position of leadership within the Edomite people. His discovery of the hot springs in the wilderness reflects a notable contribution to the community's resources and environment. These details collectively underscore his role in the historical and genealogical framework of Edom as presented in Genesis.
